target_customer: US consumers, especially underbanked savers, using a mobile bank account with weekly prize draws
problem: Many Americans save too little; the company bet that a weekly chance to win 1M dollars on debit card spending would motivate saving.
business_model: Consumer neobank with interchange revenue and prize-linked savings
product_category: Gamified mobile banking and prize-linked savings

founders.name: Agni Bhattacharya
previous_startups: Mobile word game scaled to over 1M users, IP sold to a gaming studio (game and studio not named; per YC page)
founders.background_notes: YC page: former product leader at Meta, Zynga and a Series D fintech startup; the game was a side project.

founders.name: Allison Bellows
founders.background_notes: YC page bio: into math and its siblings.

competitors.name: Yotta
competitors.what: Prize-linked savings account with weekly drawings, YC backed
competitors.traction_then: 21,000 accounts and over 40M dollars deposited about two months after its July 2020 beta

technical_complexity.rationale: A banking app needs a bank partner, KYC, card issuing and a compliant drawing mechanism, which is standard fintech engineering with regulatory complexity.

defensibility.rationale: Prize-linked savings was already offered by Yotta, and the mechanic is easy to copy.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows incumbents copying or buying Alma; the company is marked Inactive with no stated cause.

market_need_then: Prize-linked savings had precedent: the 2014 American Savings Promotion Act allows it, and Yotta reported 21,000 accounts in two months in 2020.

branding.domain_note: Uses myalmafi.com (prefix and suffix variation) per the YC page; alma.com is not claimed.

identity.voice_and_tone: Playful lottery framing in the tagline: win 1M every Wednesday

branding.community_and_virality: Crowdfunding page on Wefunder exists; no merch or community found.

brand_strength.rationale: Searches for the brand returned many unrelated Alma companies, showing the name was generic and confusable; only the weekly prize hook is distinctive.

outcome_analysis: Alma tried to win savers with a weekly 1 million dollar prize on a gamified bank account in a space already served by Yotta, and went Inactive after the Summer 2022 batch with funding reported at 500 thousand to 1.5 million dollars. No shutdown cause is public, so the brand_confusion tag is a weak inference from the generic name and not a stated reason.
notes: Cause of shutdown not public; failure factor is a weak inference. Funding conflicts: VCBacked lists 500K pre-seed Aug 2022 (single database); Wefunder snippet says 1.5M raised from Lombardstreet Ventures, Pioneer Fund, Stonks Fund, Xoogler Fund (stage and date not stated, page returned 403 and was not opened); Dealroom lists a 125K seed. Closed status for the Dealroom entry is from a search summary. Company site returned 503. Many other companies called Alma exist (Paris BNPL, others) and were excluded. Founder education not found. Long Game funding and accounts figures are from the 2017 article snippet and are not re-verified. Fixes from audit: the Wefunder round is dated 2023-05 and sized about 1.53M because Wefunder's profile lists Last Funded May 2023 with about 1.53M from 78 investors (seen via search summary; the page itself returns 403), and a single platform reports it. Kingscrowd lists the 2023 raise as a SAFE at a 15M valuation with about 41K committed in that round, which conflicts with 1.53M and is not recorded. Long Game was removed from competition_at_founding because its only source is dated 2017, five years before the 2022 founding; no better dated source was found. The Yotta entry is dated 2020, about two years before founding. The founder's prior word game and its IP sale rest on the YC page alone.
